source_name: Transparency International Hungary — Tenderbajnokok analyses
why_relevant: NGO analytical reports ranking 'tender champions' — recurring winning suppliers, single-bid rates and sectoral concentration. Not press, but the analytical backbone journalists cite; helps interpret award patterns including IT/financial services suppliers.

source_name: PosNavigator.eu blog (HU market POS provider comparisons)
why_relevant: Commercial comparison blog enumerating POS terminal / card-acquiring providers active in Hungary with pricing. Commercially motivated, but a fast map of the acquiring vendor landscape (incl. SumUp and bank acquirers) that competitive-intel needs.

source_name: Bizpay.hu blog (online payment / POS vendor blog)
why_relevant: Vendor-operated Hungarian blog on online payment and POS terminals; useful for terminology, merchant-side pain points and competitor positioning in card acceptance. Vendor bias must be flagged.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Tagjaink (member list)
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of ~40+ Hungarian banks, mortgage banks, building societies and affiliated bodies (OTP, MBH, K&H, Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, CIB, Gránit, MFB, KELER, Garantiqa, Magyar Lízingszövetség as affiliate). This is the canonical buyer-side universe for A2 tender/procurement monitoring: every entity here is a potential contracting authority or publisher of award notices.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Munkacsoportok (working groups)
why_relevant: Working-group structure (payments, IT/digitalisation, cash logistics, security etc.) reveals which functional domains banks coordinate on collectively — a leading indicator of shared/sector-wide procurement themes (instant payment, AFR 2.0, e-ID, ATM/self-service) before tenders appear.

source_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség / Hungarian Fintech Association (HFA) – Membership
why_relevant: MAFISZ/HFA aggregates the Hungarian fintech supplier ecosystem (startups, scale-ups, incubators, PSPs) that sells into banks. Membership roster enumerates likely bidders/subcontractors on Hungarian bank and payments tenders — a supplier map no public register holds.

source_name: IVSZ – Digitális Vállalkozások Szövetsége, tagvállalatok
why_relevant: IVSZ is Hungary's dominant ICT industry association; its member directory lists the IT integrators, software houses and consultancies (with membership-since dates) that bid on bank and public-sector IT tenders. Directly enumerates the vendor pool behind Hungarian financial-sector procurement.

source_name: IVSZ hírek – új tagvállalatok bejelentései (new-member news feed)
why_relevant: New-member announcements give a dated, incremental signal of which IT/consulting firms are entering the Hungarian digital-supplier market — useful for spotting emerging bidders before they appear in award notices.

source_name: Portfolio Banking Technology konferencia – Támogatók (sponsor pages, multi-year)
why_relevant: The flagship Hungarian bank-IT conference publishes tiered sponsor lists (Platinum/Super Gold/Gold/Silver/Bronze, professional and media partners) plus speaker-company rosters, per year since ~2017. Sponsor tiers are a paid, ranked signal of which vendors (e.g. 4iG, Accenture, adesso) are actively selling into Hungarian banks — a longitudinal supplier-intensity series for A2 tender targeting.

source_name: Portfolio Rendezvények – összes konferencia (event catalogue)
why_relevant: Master index of Portfolio's banking/finance/IT conference portfolio (Hitelezés, Banking Technology, Követeléskezelési trendek, etc.). Entry point for systematically harvesting every sponsor and speaker roster in the Hungarian financial-events space.

source_name: Portfolio Csoport – event-season announcements
why_relevant: Corporate-side announcements of the upcoming conference season give forward calendar visibility (which banking/payments events will run and when), enabling scheduled harvesting of sponsor lists at publication time.

source_name: IIR Hungary – Kártyapiac & Digitális fizetés konferencia és szponzoráció
why_relevant: IIR runs the long-standing 'Kártyapiac' card-market conference plus PSD2/instant-payment events; it maintains a dedicated sponsorship section listing highlighted events and their commercial partners. Audience description explicitly names card service providers, software vendors, fintechs and telcos — the payments supplier map for Hungary.

source_name: kartyapiac.hu – Kártyapiac conference programme site
why_relevant: Dedicated microsite referenced by the organiser as carrying the continuously updated Kártyapiac programme; likely host of the current-year speaker, partner and exhibitor lists for Hungary's main card/payments event.

source_name: FinTechZone – FinTechShow / BankTechShow / TechShow X. event pages
why_relevant: FinTechShow (Budapest Congress Center, ~80+ solutions in the exhibition gallery) and its successor TechShow X. publish tiered sponsor categories (Főszponzor, Arany/Ezüst/Bronz fokozatú szponzor, Kiemelt támogató, Megoldáspartner, Főtámogató) and speaker rosters. The exhibitor gallery is effectively a curated catalogue of vendors actively selling to Hungarian financial institutions.

source_name: Budapest Fintech Week (Luma / Fintech.hu listings)
why_relevant: Umbrella week of Hungarian fintech side-events; the Luma listing and Fintech.hu tag page enumerate organisers, hosts and partner companies — a route into smaller vendors and hubs that never appear on the big-conference sponsor tiers.

source_name: PayTech.Events – FINTECHSHOW Budapest listing
why_relevant: English-language aggregator entry for the Hungarian FinTechShow with dates, agenda and venue metadata; useful as an independent cross-check and for building an EN-side event calendar when the Hungarian organiser site is JS-blocked.

source_name: AmCham Hungary – Membership directory & Patron members
why_relevant: 300+ member companies with sector tagging, including banks (UniCredit, Raiffeisen), global IT vendors (IBM, T-Systems, Google, HP) and asset managers. Patron-member tiers reveal the highest-spend corporate players in Hungary — a bilingual, sector-filterable supplier/buyer directory plus an archived historical snapshot for change analysis.

source_name: DUIHK / Német-Magyar Ipari és Kereskedelmi Kamara – Tagság (member directory)
why_relevant: ~900 member companies — the largest bilateral business association in Hungary — with an online member directory. Captures German-owned banks, payment processors and IT suppliers operating in Hungary that other Hungarian-only rosters miss. Bilingual (hu/de/en) site.

source_name: MKIK – Magyar Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara (chamber registration & sections)
why_relevant: Chamber registration is mandatory for Hungarian businesses (membership is not), so the chamber system holds a near-complete registry of economic operators, searchable by county, town, activity and name. Useful for resolving and enriching supplier identities found in tender award notices, and its tagozatok (sections) map sectoral organisation.

source_name: County chamber registered-business databases (BOKIK, DKIK et al.)
why_relevant: Regional chambers expose the chamber registry through their own searchable front-ends, sometimes with different filters/exports than the national portal. Useful fallback for identifying and geolocating suppliers named in award notices.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség – Kik vagyunk / Bizottságok
why_relevant: 36 member asset-finance companies (leasing firms, banks, financial enterprises) financing ~500k individuals and 200k businesses. An adjacent-sector buyer list for payments/IT procurement, and its committee structure names the active practitioner network. Also an affiliate member of Magyar Bankszövetség (cross-link confirmed).

source_name: Blockchain Magyarország Egyesület
why_relevant: Founding member of the Hungarian Blockchain Coalition and consortium member of the DigitalTech EDIH project; its partner and coalition affiliations point to public-sector-facing digital consortia that bid for or shape state and financial-sector digital tenders.

source_name: i40platform.hu – szervezet/tagok (Industry 4.0 platform member organisations)
why_relevant: A state-linked platform whose member list includes IVSZ and DUIHK; it aggregates associations and companies in one place, which is a useful cross-index for discovering further Hungarian trade bodies relevant to digital and financial-sector procurement.

source_name: NJSZT iTF Adattár – institutional history of Hungarian IT associations
why_relevant: The Neumann Society's IT-history archive documents Hungarian IT trade bodies and companies over decades, including predecessor names and mergers. Valuable for resolving legacy vendor names appearing in older award notices and for tracing corporate lineage.

source_name: LinkedIn company pages of Hungarian banking/fintech associations
why_relevant: Association and chamber LinkedIn pages publish event announcements, sponsor tags and partner mentions that are often not mirrored on the main websites, and surface the individuals brokering vendor-bank relationships.

source_name: bankweb.hu – IIR Kártyapiac conference coverage
why_relevant: Trade-press coverage of the card-market conference that describes the participant profile (banks, card service providers, fintechs, telcos, cafeteria-card issuers, government agencies). Useful for reconstructing attendee/vendor composition when organiser sponsor pages are archived away.

source_name: Profession.hu - Hungary's largest job board (bank/insurance/broker category)
why_relevant: Bank and vendor job ads naming a platform (core banking, card system, instant payment) or a named programme are the earliest fingerprint of an awarded or upcoming IT/payments contract. Category+keyword URLs are stable and filterable by employer.
